findings.title: order mixin off-by-one for legacy box-ordinal-group
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss the order() mixin copies $val directly into -webkit-box-ordinal-group and -moz-box-ordinal-group. The legacy 2009 box ordinal-group is 1-based (default 1 corresponds to modern order 0), so correct fallback is $val + 1. As written @include order(2) / order(3) in header/topic emit ordinal-group 2/3 which mean modern order 1/2, so legacy WebKit/Firefox order header elements differently than modern browsers, and any future order(1) will tie with the default group 1 and not reorder at all in legacy browsers.

findings.title: float:right on flex item is ignored, action button not right-aligned
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/topic-post.scss .small-action is now a flex container, making .topic-avatar, .small-action-desc and button flex items. Per CSS Flexbox spec float has no effect on flex items, so button { float: right; } is dead. The button will sit immediately after the description instead of at the far right edge, crowding text and breaking the previous small-action layout. It needs margin-left: auto or justify-content handling, not float.

findings.title: margin-left:auto fallback fails with 2009 flexbox prefixes
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/base/header.scss .panel uses margin-left: auto to push it right inside .contents which uses the new flexbox() mixin. That mixin emits display: -webkit-box / -moz-box 2009 fallbacks where auto margins do not absorb free space or push items to the end. In browsers that only understand those prefixed values the header panel will not be right-aligned and will collapse next to the title, breaking the header the mixin claims to support.

findings.title: align-items mixin emits invalid property and misses Firefox prefix
findings.body: In app/assets/stylesheets/common/foundation/mixins.scss align-items() emits -ms-align-items which does not exist and is dead code, while omitting -moz-box-align even though flexbox() emits display: -moz-box. Old Firefox therefore gets a legacy flex container with no alignment declaration and loses the vertical centering/baseline alignment used for the header and bullet badges. The mixin also forwards modern values verbatim to -ms-flex-align/-webkit-box-align whose keyword sets differ, inviting future misuse.
